papers.title: A systems biology network analysis of root resorption biomarkers and their clinical relevance in orthodontics: a pilot study.
papers.abstract: External apical root resorption is a frequently reported iatrogenic consequence of orthodontic tooth movement. This pilot study used an integrated systems biology approach to identify signaling pathways, key genes, and candidate salivary biomarkers associated with orthodontic root resorption to support future functional research.
papers.summary: This pilot study applies systems biology network analysis to identify signaling pathways, key genes, and candidate salivary biomarkers linked to orthodontic root resorption. The findings aim to guide future functional research and potential clinical biomarker development in orthodontics.

papers.title: Endothelial SLC25A13 links glutamine metabolism to angiogenesis.
papers.abstract: Attention to exploring endothelial cell (EC) metabolism is increasing, but a holistic perspective on the metabolic adaptations of ECs during angiogenic proliferation is still missing. Here, we use a previously in-house developed computational EC-adapted genome-scale metabolic model that recapitulates known metabolic features in proliferating ECs to predict novel pathways central to biomass synthesis. We unveil the metabolic function of the glutamate-aspartate antiporter SLC25A13, previously overlooked in ECs, as a key regulator of glutamine utilization and provide evidence regarding its contri
papers.summary: Using a computational genome-scale metabolic model tailored to endothelial cells, the authors predicted and validated that the mitochondrial glutamate-aspartate antiporter SLC25A13 is a key regulator of glutamine utilization during angiogenesis. This previously overlooked transporter links glutamine metabolism to endothelial proliferation, revealing a new metabolic vulnerability in blood vessel formation.

papers.title: Enhancing 3-hydroxypropionic acid production in Komagataella phaffii via methanol and formate co-feeding.
papers.abstract: Komagataella phaffii is a promising cell factory that can use CO2 derived methanol, a sustainable carbon (C1) source, for chemical production. Introducing the ß-alanine biosynthetic pathway alongside a NADP+-dependent formate dehydrogenase (FDH) in K. phaffii enables the production of the platform chemical 3-hydroxypropionic acid (3-HP). Co-feeding of formate and methanol (MeOH) was systematically explored to enhance cellular reducing power and improve 3-HP biosynthesis. Implementing a pulsed formate strategy alongside MeOH resulted in up to a 20.7% increase in 3-HP per gram of MeOH (Yg3-HP gM
papers.summary: This study engineers Komagataella phaffii to produce 3-hydroxypropionic acid (3-HP) from methanol by introducing a β-alanine pathway and a NADP+-dependent formate dehydrogenase. Co-feeding formate with methanol in a pulsed strategy boosts cellular reducing power, increasing 3-HP yield per gram of methanol by up to 20.7%. The work demonstrates a metabolic engineering approach to improve C1-based chemical production.

papers.title: Harnessing computational intelligence for synthetic lethality: A roadmap from network biology to interpretable deep learning in precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Synthetic lethality (SL) is an emerging therapeutic paradigm in precision oncology that enables the selective targeting of cancer cells based on their specific genetic vulnerabilities. Despite its clinical promise, the enormous combinatorial search space of gene-gene interactions poses a major challenge for experimental screening. This review provides a critical survey of computational SL discovery, moving beyond sequential descriptions to offer a comparative synthesis of architectures ranging from traditional network-based models to advanced graph transformers and knowledge graph reasoning. W
papers.summary: This review surveys computational approaches for predicting synthetic lethal gene pairs in cancer, comparing traditional network-based models with modern deep learning architectures like graph transformers and knowledge graph reasoning. It argues that interpretable deep learning can help navigate the vast combinatorial search space of gene-gene interactions to identify new therapeutic targets in precision oncology.

papers.title: Enterobacteriaceae for succinic acid biomanufacturing: metabolic blueprints, systems-level engineering and future perspectives.
papers.abstract: Succinic acid (SA) is a key C4 platform molecule with wide industrial relevance, including bio-based polymers and solvents. Current reviews largely emphasize traditional producers (e.g., Actinobacillus, Mannheimia, and Basfia) and rarely synthesize progress in Enterobacteriaceae. Here, we close this gap by providing a systems-level review of SA biomanufacturing in Enterobacteriaceae, focusing on non-model genera (Enterobacter, Klebsiella, Citrobacter) that combine fast growth, facultative anaerobiosis, broad feedstock utilization, and high engineering amenability. We outline the metabolic blue
papers.summary: This review synthesizes progress in engineering Enterobacteriaceae (Enterobacter, Klebsiella, Citrobacter) for succinic acid biomanufacturing, highlighting their fast growth, facultative anaerobiosis, and broad feedstock utilization. It provides metabolic blueprints and systems-level engineering strategies, positioning these non-model genera as promising alternatives to traditional producers like Actinobacillus and Mannheimia.

papers.title: Integrative Proteomics and Genome-Scale Modeling Elucidate Metabolic Flux Shifts in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii CC-4414 Under Light Stress.
papers.abstract: The green microalga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii holds substantial promise as a photosynthetic cell factory for sustainable bioproduction, yet strain-specific metabolic responses to environmental stress remain underexplored. Here, we reconstructed a genome-scale metabolic network (GSMN) of the light-tolerant strain C. reinhardtii CC-4414 by combining de novo genome assembly with integrative proteomics. The resulting model, designated iYH2021, comprises 2021 genes, 2601 reactions, and 2089 metabolites, representing the first genome-scale metabolic reconstruction reported for this strain. To elucid
papers.summary: The authors reconstructed the first genome-scale metabolic model for the light-tolerant Chlamydomonas reinhardtii strain CC-4414 by combining de novo genome assembly with proteomics, producing a model (iYH2021) with 2021 genes, 2601 reactions, and 2089 metabolites. Using this model, they analyzed metabolic flux shifts under light stress, revealing strain-specific adaptations that could inform engineering of algae as photosynthetic cell factories.

papers.title: MAPA: A Semantic Network Framework for Functional Module Discovery and Interpretation in Multi-Omics Data.
papers.abstract: Multi-omics technologies generate high-dimensional molecular signatures that provide unprecedented opportunities to uncover biological mechanisms. However, translating complex molecular alterations into coherent and interpretable functional insights remains a major challenge. Existing module discovery methods can identify groups of related features, but often lack direct biological interpretability, whereas pathway-based approaches frequently yield redundant results that complicate interpretation. Here, we present MAPA (Modular Analysis and Phenotype-informed Annotation using large language mo
papers.summary: MAPA is a semantic network framework that integrates multi-omics data with large language models to discover and interpret functional modules. It addresses the limitations of existing module discovery methods, which often lack biological interpretability, and pathway-based approaches, which can produce redundant results. The framework aims to translate complex molecular alterations into coherent, interpretable functional insights.

papers.title: Protamine gene expression is associated with sperm motility in rams: An integrative experimental and gene network analysis.
papers.abstract: Protamine 1 (PRM1) and protamine 2 (PRM2) are essential regulators of sperm chromatin condensation and genome integrity, and their dysregulation has been associated with impaired male fertility. However, their role in rams remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the relationship between protamine gene expression and semen quality in rams and explored their potential upstream regulatory mechanisms using gene regulatory network (GRN) analysis. Fifteen ejaculates from five rams were analyzed. Based on total sperm motility using computer-assisted sperm analysis (CASA), ejacul
papers.summary: This study examined how expression of the protamine genes PRM1 and PRM2 relates to semen quality in rams, analyzing 15 ejaculates from five animals. Higher protamine gene expression was associated with better total sperm motility, and gene regulatory network analysis was used to identify potential upstream regulators of these genes. The findings suggest protamines may serve as markers of sperm quality in this livestock species.

papers.title: KBase: Open-source Platform for Collaborative Biological Data Analysis and Publication.
papers.abstract: The U.S. Department of Energy's Systems Biology Knowledgebase (KBase; www.kbase.us) is an open, collaborative platform that integrates data, models, and analysis tools to accelerate discovery in microbiology, plant biology, and environmental systems. Recently, KBase expanded as a comprehensive, multi-omics ecosystem. KBase enables representation of scientific samples, long-read sequence analysis, protein structure integration, and scalable modeling of microbial communities across diverse environments. KBase also generates digital notebooks as citable, executable research objects that link data
papers.summary: KBase is an open-source, collaborative platform that integrates multi-omics data, models, and analysis tools to accelerate discovery in microbiology, plant biology, and environmental systems. Recent expansions add long-read sequence analysis, protein structure integration, scalable microbial community modeling, and citable executable digital notebooks. It serves as a comprehensive ecosystem for reproducible, collaborative biological data analysis and publication.

papers.title: GLM-Prior: a genomic language model for transferable sequence-derived priors in gene regulatory network inference.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference depends on high-quality prior knowledge, yet curated priors are often incomplete or unavailable across species and cell types. We present GLM-Prior, a genomic language model fine-tuned to predict transcription factor-target gene interactions from nucleotide sequence. We integrate GLM-Prior with PMF-GRN in a dual-stage pipeline that combines sequence-derived priors with single-cell expression data for prior-conditioned GRN inference. Across six cell-line contexts, GLM-Prior performance scales with positive label abundance and TF coverage, showing above-chance a
papers.summary: GLM-Prior is a genomic language model fine-tuned to predict transcription factor-target gene interactions directly from nucleotide sequence, providing transferable priors where curated knowledge is incomplete. Integrated with PMF-GRN in a dual-stage pipeline, it combines sequence-derived priors with single-cell expression data for prior-conditioned gene regulatory network inference across six cell-line contexts.

papers.title: Integrative Multi-Omics Analysis Reveals Host Regulatory and Immune Networks with Inferred Dysbiosis Relevance in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Background: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Increasing evidence suggests that intestinal microbial dysbiosis contributes to colorectal tumorigenesis by reshaping host molecular signaling and the tumor immune microenvironment. However, the molecular mechanisms linking microbiome-associated alterations to host regulatory networks and disease progression remain incompletely understood. Objective: This study aimed to identify the microbiome-associated molecular regulators and immune modulators involved in colorectal cancer through an
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to identify host regulatory and immune networks in colorectal cancer that are associated with inferred microbial dysbiosis. It highlights candidate molecular regulators and immune modulators linking microbiome alterations to tumor progression, though the dysbiosis inference is computational rather than directly measured.

papers.title: Selection favors cost-ordered adaptive mutational paths in a stress-magnitude-dependent manner.
papers.abstract: Chronic exposure to stress requires adaptive strategies beyond canonical regulatory mechanisms. Stress varies, both qualitatively and quantitatively, across physiological niches and exerts distinct selection pressures on colonizing bacteria. Bacteria employ diverse defense strategies to withstand various stressful conditions, yet how they tailor their responses to different magnitudes of the same stressor remains poorly understood. We used multiple adaptive laboratory evolution experiments of Escherichia coli across varying paraquat concentrations and genetic backgrounds to dissect adaptive st
papers.summary: This study uses adaptive laboratory evolution of E. coli under different concentrations of the oxidative stressor paraquat to show that selection favors mutational paths ordered by their fitness cost, and that this ordering depends on stress magnitude. The findings reveal how bacteria tailor adaptive strategies quantitatively to the intensity of the same stressor.

papers.title: Integrated Cell-Based Transcriptomic and Pathway Profiling Enables Scalable Functional Screening of Bioactive Microalgal Extracts.
papers.abstract: Background: Microalgae and cyanobacteria represent a largely unexplored source of bioactive compounds, but systematic screening of extensive strain collections is limited by the cost and complexity of conventional chemical and pharmacological characterization. Here, we evaluated a scalable functional screening strategy integrating human cell-based gene expression profiling, quantitative molecular pathway analysis, and direct cytotoxicity testing to prioritize bioactive microalgal and cyanobacterial extracts for subsequent investigation. Results: Forty-eight extracts were screened using HL-60 h
papers.summary: This study presents a scalable screening pipeline that combines human cell-based transcriptomic profiling, pathway analysis, and cytotoxicity testing to prioritize bioactive compounds from microalgae and cyanobacteria. Screening 48 extracts in HL-60 cells demonstrates that integrated functional profiling can efficiently identify promising natural product candidates without exhaustive chemical characterization.

papers.title: Uncovering combination therapies for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases through systems biology analysis on longitudinal patient data.
papers.abstract: While targeted therapies have reshaped the clinical management of immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs), primary non-response remains a major obstacle for many patients. Combining two targeted therapies is an emerging strategy to overcome this therapeutic ceiling, but the number of possible drug pairs makes prioritization difficult. For this objective, we present mitigation of non-response signature (MNRS), a computational approach that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from six IMIDs treated with different targeted therapies to identify the most promising drug combinations.
papers.summary: The authors present MNRS, a computational systems-biology method that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from six immune-mediated inflammatory diseases to prioritize combination therapies for patients who fail to respond to single targeted drugs. By identifying drug pairs that counteract non-response signatures, the approach narrows down the vast space of possible combinations to the most promising candidates.

papers.title: Metabolic modeling with reverse mapping links host perturbations to Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
papers.abstract: Understanding host-pathogen interactions during Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection has largely relied on identifying bacterial genes essential for intracellular survival. However, conventional reverse genetics approaches often overlook host pathways that regulate Mtb growth. Here, we developed a backtracing strategy to link host metabolic modulators with specific Mtb proteins. A genome-scale host metabolic model integrated with lung transcriptomic data from H37Rv-infected mice predicted 18 host proteins essential for Mtb survival. We validated this through pharmacological inhibition, s
papers.summary: The authors developed a backtracing strategy that integrates a genome-scale host metabolic model with lung transcriptomic data from Mtb-infected mice to identify host proteins that influence bacterial survival. They predicted 18 host proteins essential for Mtb survival and validated these predictions through pharmacological inhibition. This approach links host metabolic perturbations to specific Mtb proteins, offering a new way to uncover host-directed therapeutic targets.

papers.title: CardamomOT: A mechanistic optimal transport-based framework for gene regulatory network inference, trajectory reconstruction and generative modeling.
papers.abstract: A key challenge in inferring gene regulatory networks (GRNs) governing cellular processes such as differentiation and reprogramming from experimental data lies in the impossibility of directly measuring protein dynamics at the single-cell level, which prevents establishing causal relationships between regulator activity and target responses. In earlier work, we introduced CARDAMOM, an algorithm that uses temporal snapshots of scRNA-seq data to calibrate a GRN-driven mechanistic model of gene expression. However, this method had several limitations: it could only rely on the relative ordering o
papers.summary: The authors present CardamomOT, a mechanistic optimal transport framework that infers gene regulatory networks, reconstructs differentiation trajectories, and enables generative modeling from single-cell RNA-seq data. It extends their earlier CARDAMOM algorithm by using optimal transport to overcome limitations of relying only on relative temporal ordering, allowing more robust causal inference of regulator-target relationships.

papers.title: Whole-cell spatiotemporal model and multimodal data illuminate the multiscale light responses in a photosynthetic bacterium.
papers.abstract: Photosynthetic microorganisms rely on multiple central carbon metabolism pathways to adapt to fluctuating light and energy availability across diel cycles. Mechanistic insight into the regulatory dynamics of this adaptation requires integrating processes that operate across disparate timescales, from rapid redox-dependent post-translational modifications (PTMs) to slower changes in protein expression and metabolic pathway usage. Here, we develop a whole-cell 4D (3D + time) model of the marine cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus marinus MED4 that explicitly represents the spatial, subcellular organi
papers.summary: This paper presents a whole-cell 4D (3D + time) computational model of the marine cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus marinus MED4, integrating spatial subcellular organization with multiscale regulatory processes. The model captures light responses spanning rapid redox-dependent post-translational modifications to slower changes in protein expression and metabolic pathway usage, and is combined with multimodal data to illuminate these dynamics. It offers a framework for understanding how photosynthetic microorganisms adapt to fluctuating light across diel cycles.

papers.title: Rhizobia bacteroid transcription helps to coordinate the soybean nodule drought response.
papers.abstract: Soybean (Glycine max L. [Merr.]) nitrogen fixation is sensitive to soil drying and is an important target for improving soybean drought resilience. Transcriptional regulation of the nodule drought response and the influence of symbiotic rhizobia are not well understood. We measured whole-plant responses to mild and moderate soil moisture deficit (41% and 20% of field capacity) alongside the nodule transcriptome, including soybean and Bradyrhizobium diazoefficiens transcripts, in two soybean genotypes ('Benning' and PI 471938) that were previously found to have diverging nitrogen fixation droug
papers.summary: This study examined how soybean nodules respond to mild and moderate drought at the transcriptome level, capturing both soybean and its symbiotic rhizobia (Bradyrhizobium diazoefficiens) gene expression in two genotypes with differing drought tolerance. The findings suggest that rhizobia bacteroid transcription actively helps coordinate the nodule drought response, highlighting the symbiotic partner's role in nitrogen fixation resilience under water deficit.

papers.title: Thermo-flux: generation and analysis of thermodynamic-stoichiometric metabolic network models.
papers.abstract: Metabolic modeling with stoichiometric models and flux balance analysis (FBA) has greatly advanced our understanding of metabolism. However, valid FBA predictions require mechanistically correct constraints. Thermodynamic constraints can increase the mechanistic foundations of stoichiometric models and reduce the solution space, but incorporating them has so far required cumbersome manual effort. To circumvent manual curation, we introduce 'Thermo-Flux', a semi-automated Python package that converts stoichiometric models into comprehensive thermodynamic-stoichiometric models. 'Thermo-Flux' ena
papers.summary: Thermo-Flux is a semi-automated Python package that converts standard stoichiometric metabolic models into thermodynamic-stoichiometric models, adding thermodynamic constraints without the usual manual curation burden. This allows flux balance analysis predictions to be more mechanistically grounded and narrows the feasible solution space, improving the reliability of metabolic modeling.

papers.title: From plasmid sequence to process design: A computational analysis of metabolism in the context of plasmid DNA manufacturing.
papers.abstract: Detailed understanding of plasmid-host physiological interactions and recombinant protein expression is crucial for the design and optimization of plasmid DNA (pDNA) manufacturing processes. Successfully transformed host cells carrying one or more copies of a particular plasmid exhibit modified metabolic behavior which may include reduced specific growth rate, increased metabolic resource cycling (ATP/ADP, NAD/NADH, NADP/NADPH) and, in some cases, even modified nutrient uptake and metabolite secretion rates. Mapping plasmid design features to critical process parameters (CPPs), such as specifi
papers.summary: This paper uses computational metabolic modeling to analyze how plasmid DNA (pDNA) production alters host cell physiology, including growth rate, energy cofactor cycling, and nutrient uptake/secretion. The authors aim to connect specific plasmid design features to critical process parameters, providing a framework for rational design and optimization of pDNA manufacturing processes.

papers.title: Systems biology-driven drug repurposing in glioblastoma via antigen and pathway mapping.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive brain tumor with limited treatment options and poor patient survival. This study aimed to identify key genes and altered pathways in GBM and to explore potential drug-repurposing candidates using a systems biology approach.
papers.summary: This study applies a systems biology approach to glioblastoma, integrating gene expression and pathway data to identify key altered genes and pathways, then maps these to candidate drugs for repurposing. The goal is to find existing drugs that could be redirected to treat this aggressive brain tumor, which currently has few effective options.

papers.title: Biological limits of lifespan extension: Evidence for a shift from pathway leverage to system-level buffering across species.
papers.abstract: Interventions targeting conserved aging pathways can markedly extend lifespan in model organisms, yet their efficacy declines with increasing organismal complexity. While this phenomenon is well documented, the underlying constraints remain poorly defined. Here, we integrate comparative experimental data with mechanistic insights to propose a unifying framework explaining the declining ceiling of lifespan extension. We show that in simple organisms, aging is governed by a limited number of high-leverage pathways, whereas in mammals it emerges from distributed, multi-tissue regulatory systems c
papers.summary: This review proposes a unifying framework to explain why interventions targeting conserved aging pathways extend lifespan dramatically in simple organisms but only modestly in mammals. The authors argue that aging shifts from being governed by a few high-leverage pathways in simple organisms to a distributed, multi-tissue regulatory system in mammals, where system-level buffering limits further gains. This reframes the declining ceiling of lifespan extension as an inherent consequence of increasing organismal complexity.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: This paper introduces a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, using a gradient-boosted meta-classifier trained on the raw scores from ten different inference methods to decide which method to trust for each candidate regulator-target pair. The authors also propose a diagnostic typology for characterizing conflicts between methods, moving beyond the common practice of picking one method or averaging all of them.

papers.title: Cell dynamics on energy landscape: Comparing attractor detection in Boolean network and diffusion-based models under in silico gene perturbations.
papers.abstract: Steady-state attractor detection differs fundamentally between discrete Boolean network (BN) and continuous diffusion-based models because they operate on different state spaces and exhibit distinct dynamic behaviors. Here, we propose cell dynamics on energy landscape (CellLand) to systematically compare BN and diffusion-based approaches for quantifying cellular dynamics on the energy landscape, with a particular focus on attractor identification under in silico gene perturbations. Although the energy landscape provides a unifying conceptual framework, BN-based models face specific challenges,
papers.summary: This paper introduces CellLand, a framework for comparing how Boolean network and diffusion-based models identify steady-state attractors on an energy landscape under simulated gene perturbations. It highlights that while the energy landscape offers a unifying conceptual view, discrete Boolean models face specific challenges in this comparison. The work aims to clarify when each modeling approach is appropriate for quantifying cellular dynamics.

papers.title: GP-DHT: A dual-head transformer with supervised contrastive learning for shared-gene pretraining and single-cell GRN prediction.
papers.abstract: Gene Regulatory Networks (GRNs) are crucial for understanding cell fate decisions and disease mechanisms. However, inferring GRNs from single-cell RNA sequencing remains challenging due to noise, data sparsity, and species-specific distribution variations. We propose GP-DHT (Gene Pair-Dual Head Transformer), a single-cell GRN inference framework that pre-trains gene representations on a unified shared gene space using the BEELINE datasets of humans and mice. It models gene-cell expression relationships through a multi-relational heterograph and predicts transcription factor (TF)-target regulat
papers.summary: GP-DHT is a dual-head transformer framework that pre-trains gene representations on a shared human-mouse gene space using supervised contrastive learning, then predicts transcription factor-target regulatory relationships from single-cell RNA-seq data. It models gene-cell expression via a multi-relational heterograph to address noise, sparsity, and cross-species distribution shifts in GRN inference.

papers.title: Single-cell virtual knockout network perturbation prioritizes candidate regulators of beta-cell functional failure in type 2 diabetes.
papers.abstract: Progressive pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction is a central feature of type 2 diabetes (T2D), but disease-associated transcriptional changes alone cannot distinguish likely regulatory drivers from secondary stress markers. Single-cell transcriptomics resolves beta-cell heterogeneity across disease states, while virtual-knockout network analysis estimates transcriptional effects after perturbing selected genes. We combined human islet single-cell RNA sequencing, beta-cell functional-state modeling, candidate scoring, scTenifoldKnk virtual knockout, and external validation to prioritize regulators
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing of human pancreatic islets with virtual-knockout network perturbation analysis to distinguish regulatory drivers of beta-cell failure in type 2 diabetes from passive stress markers. By combining functional-state modeling, candidate scoring, and scTenifoldKnk, the authors prioritize candidate regulators and validate them externally. The approach offers a framework for moving beyond correlative transcriptomic changes to causal regulatory hypotheses in T2D.

papers.title: Host-directed therapeutics against antimicrobial-resistant bacterial infections: emerging roles of multi-omics and systems biology.
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence and global dissemination of antimicrobial resistance (AMR), coupled with the limited development of new antimicrobial agents, have intensified concerns regarding a major global public health crisis. Although antibiotic resistance is primarily driven by microbial mechanisms, host immune and inflammatory responses also play critical roles in determining infection outcomes, pathogen persistence, and treatment efficacy. In this context, host-directed therapies (HDTs) have emerged as a promising complementary strategy by modulating host pathways to enhance antimicrobial immunity
papers.summary: This review discusses how host-directed therapies (HDTs) can complement traditional antibiotics by modulating the host's immune and inflammatory responses to combat antimicrobial-resistant infections. It highlights the emerging role of multi-omics and systems biology approaches in identifying host pathways and biomarkers that can be targeted for therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: Neuro-psycho MMSig: multimodal mechanism enrichment platform for neuropsychiatric disorders.
papers.abstract: Understanding the pathophysiology of neurodegenerative and psychiatric disorders requires integrating multimodal data.
papers.summary: The authors present Neuro-psycho MMSig, a computational platform designed to integrate multimodal data for studying the mechanisms underlying neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders. The tool aims to enrich mechanistic insights by combining diverse data types, addressing the challenge of understanding complex brain disorders. This work provides a resource for researchers seeking to uncover convergent pathophysiological pathways across multiple data modalities.

papers.title: Evolution, disciplinary integration, and frontiers of multi-omics and single-cell technologies in periodontology: a bibliometric analysis (2000-2025) with an early-2026 frontier update.
papers.abstract: The field of periodontology is undergoing a paradigm shift from traditional microbiology to systems biology, driven by advancements in multi-omics and single-cell technologies. Despite the rapid surge in publications, a Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC)-based bibliometric and scientometric analysis mapping the evolutionary trajectory and emerging frontiers of these technologies in periodontal research remains needed. We performed a bibliometric and scientometric analysis of literature published from 2000 to 2025, with records from early 2026 used only as an exploratory frontier update, us
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis maps the evolution of multi-omics and single-cell technologies in periodontology research from 2000 to 2025, showing a shift from traditional microbiology toward systems biology approaches. It identifies publication trends, disciplinary integration patterns, and emerging research frontiers, with an exploratory update from early 2026.

papers.title: Probiogenomics as a Computational Biotechnology Framework: Safety-Gated Genome Analytics for Candidate Probiotic Prioritization and Validation.
papers.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing has transformed probiotic discovery into a strain-resolved computational problem, but genome data alone cannot establish probiotic efficacy, complete safety, or regulatory acceptability. This review frames probiogenomics as a safety-gated decision-support framework for candidate probiotic prioritization and validation. The framework integrates strain provenance, genome quality, strain authentication, taxonomic confidence, antimicrobial resistance screening, virulence and toxin assessment, plasmid, prophage and mobile-element analysis, undesirable metabolite screening, f
papers.summary: This review proposes probiogenomics as a computational framework that uses whole-genome sequencing data to prioritize and validate probiotic candidates, with safety screening as a mandatory gate. It integrates analyses such as strain authentication, taxonomic confidence, antimicrobial resistance, virulence factors, mobile elements, and undesirable metabolite production. The authors emphasize that genomic data alone cannot prove probiotic efficacy or regulatory acceptability, so the framework serves as decision support rather than a standalone verdict.
